messages:
ops-bot: PAGER — high GPU queue growth on gpu-serve-prod. Autoscaler reporting failures to create nodes. Alert threshold crossed (queue > 800, throttling tokens spiking). Paging oncall.
maya: I'm oncall. saw the alert in Dash. digging into cluster-autoscaler logs now.
chris: grabbing context — are customers seeing 5xx or rate-limited responses?
maya: some generation requests are getting 429s from the frontend edge (we're throttling when no GPU capacity). Most are queued for >60s. Putting customer-impact tag "degraded" for now.
maya: cluster-autoscaler events:

```
I0403 14:10:12.345678       1 scale_up.go:xxx] Failed to scale up: failed to create node group: CreateAutoScalingGroup: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/infra-autoscaler-role is not authorized to perform: autoscaling:CreateOrUpdateTags on resource: arn:aws:autoscaling:us-west-2:123456789012:autoScalingGroup:xxxx
---
W0403 14:10:12.345678       1 utils.go:xxx] LaunchTemplate validation failed: launchTemplateSpec mismatch: iamInstanceProfile missing
```

maya: autoscaler is trying to use the launch template that doesn't include the instance profile the node bootstrap requires — so EC2 creation fails. also seeing taint mismatch logs: nodes would be created with taint gpu=reserved:NoSchedule but our GPU pods require toleration gpu-workload:NoSchedule (label name mismatch).
jordan: ugh — this smells like recent launch-template change from infra team. @infra-bot did we just push a LT update to gpu nodegroups last night?
infra-bot: CHANGELOG: launch-template gpu-lt-v3 deployed 2026-04-03 01:22 UTC. Changes: removed legacy instance profile "redwood-instance-profile", replaced with arn:aws:iam::123456789012:instance-profile/restricted-profile.
chris: that explains the AccessDenied. cluster-autoscaler role still assumes it can create nodes with the old profile. Need either to update autoscaler to use new launch template or roll back LT.
maya: short-term mitigation: 1) reduce batch concurrency to lower queue growth; 2) drain low-priority jobs (sched class "best-effort") 3) open temporary extra capacity by manually creating a nodegroup with correct IAM/instance-profile.
maya: applying immediate traffic control — lowering user concurrency from 6 -> 2 for hosted tier. Will push config in 2 min.
chris: I'll open a manual ASG using gpu-lt-v4 (we have a copy with the correct profile) and attach k8s labels/tolerations matching the scheduled pods. Creating ASG now.

```
# aws cli snippet
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name redwood-temp-gpu-001 --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd1234 --min-size 0 --max-size 10 --desired-capacity 3 --vpc-zone-identifier "subnet-..."
```

chris: hitting IAM error when trying to attach instance profile via API — hitting same policy boundary for infra-autoscaler role. escalating to infra-iam.
jordan: if infra-iam ETA > 30m we should side-step: provision nodes using a bootstrap script that attaches required kube labels and tolerations post-boot and let them join as untainted nodes, then patch pods to tolerate.
maya: creating a quick NodePool manifest to patch node labels/tolerations when node joins. Also adding this to incident notes so we can revert.
chris: infra-iam responded — they reverted LT rollout to include previous instance-profile permissions for autoscaler role. They say they pushed policy change and will validate in ~8 minutes.
maya: cluster-autoscaler logs showing backoff; but now seeing CreateFleet succeed for a couple attempts. New nodes booting.

```
I0403 14:22:58.987654       1 scale_up.go:xxx] Created 3 nodes (redwood-temp-gpu-001) for node group gpu-prod-az-a
I0403 14:23:25.123456       1 nodes.go:xxx] Node "ip-10-0-1-234" registered, labels: "kubernetes.io/arch=amd64, node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=g4dn.xlarge, redwood/gpu=true"
```

chris: added toleration mapping script and patched DaemonSet so GPU pods accept gpu-workload or gpu=reserved taints. rolling patch now.
maya: evicting non-critical pods from newly created nodes to free GPUs for serving. low-priority job queue backfilled.
jordan: monitoring queue — 10m after manual nodes up, queue down from 820 -> 120. throttling decreased, 429s dropping.
maya: doing handoff note — I'm primary until 14:30 PST. @chris you'll be primary once I escalate to post-incident review. Leaving incident running while infra finishes config rollback and we validate healer fixes.
chris: when we stabilize we need a 3-point follow-up:
- Ensure launch-template change process includes autoscaler role checks and instance-profile validation
- Add autoscaler pre-check that validates LT has required IAM instance profile and correct taints/tolerations labels
- Add dashboard alert for autoscaler CreateNodeGroup errors (AccessDenied / LaunchTemplate mismatch)
infra-bot: POLICY: rolled back change id 2026-04-03-gpu-lt. New policy applied to allow autoscaling service role to create ASG with instance-profile redwood-instance-profile. Monitor for 15m.
maya: status update: impacted pods (99th latency) improved to baseline; customers seeing degraded -> mostly okay. marking incident state: mitigated.
chris: cleanup plan: 1) remove temporary ASG redwood-temp-gpu-001 in 1h after tombstone of ephemeral workloads 2) schedule postmortem 1pm PT tomorrow with infra and SRE 3) PR to autoscaler config for LT validation.
maya: adding incident severity and TTR to ticket. moving to handoff channel. thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident #INC-2026-04-03-07
